Housing assistance / 4–6 min

What does it take
to find a home
with a voucher?

Rental assistance is an important beginning. Follow the distance between approval and a signed lease.

By Megan Quigley · A synthesis of published research

Follow the story ↓

From approval to a front-door key

01 Benefit02 Search03 Barriers04 Leases05 Support06 Delivery

01 / Benefit

Approved

A housing voucher helps pay the rent. A local agency pays part to the landlord; the household pays its share.

Approval starts a new task: finding a home where that help can be used.

HUD: how housing vouchers work ↗

02 / Search

Now find somewhere to use it

Find a home. Agree with a landlord. Complete the paperwork.

The agency checks the home and rent before the lease and assistance arrangements are completed.

Three parties must coordinate before the search deadline. Extensions depend on the local agency.

HUD: searching, tenancy approval, and extensions ↗

03 / Barriers

The doors that stay closed

A listing is not always an open door.

In this five-location study, voucher denial ranged from 15% to 78%. Scroll to compare the doors that closed.

These historical acceptance tests measure one barrier—not completed leases or current local rules.

Urban Institute: five-site landlord acceptance study, published 2018 ↗

04 / Leases

From voucher to lease

Follow 100 new voucher searches.

About 57 recorded a lease within one year in 2022. About 43 did not record that outcome.

The exact lease-up estimate fell from 65.7% in 2020 to 57.3% in 2022. These records show the gap, not every reason behind it.

Furman Center: sample and one-year success rates, pages 8–10 ↗

05 / Support

Help with the search

What if the voucher came with practical search support?

In a Seattle–King County trial, 15% of the control group moved to high-upward-mobility neighborhoods. With a bundle of support, 53% did.

This measures neighborhood choice—not the overall chance of finding any home.

Opportunity Insights: Creating Moves to Opportunity randomized trial ↗

06 / Delivery

What counts as delivery?

The voucher is a commitment. The key is a usable benefit.

Measure what happens after approval: the search, the obstacles, and the lease.

What this story can tell us

This story begins after a voucher is issued. The 2022 outcome is a one-year lease-up estimate at agencies passing data-quality checks. The landlord study and neighborhood trial have different populations and outcomes. None measures access among everyone eligible for housing assistance.

Illustrations explain a process. They do not depict an interviewed person. Recommendations and editorial questions are labeled separately from measured results.
